titulo: Linkers: although, in spite of, despite
descripcion_es: Although, even though, despite, in spite of, whereas, while, however, nevertheless: which structure follows each one.
resumen: Contrast connectors are distinguished by what follows them: although/even though go with a clause; despite/in spite of with a noun or -ing; however and nevertheless link two sentences; whereas/while compare two opposite facts.

filas: Although it was raining, we went out.
Despite the rain, we went out. In spite of feeling ill, she came.
despite the fact that / in spite of the fact that
Despite the fact that it was raining, we went out.
new sentence (after a full stop or semicolon, with a comma)
It was raining. However, we went out.
My sister loves cities, whereas I prefer the countryside.
It was cheap, yet it worked perfectly.

explicacion.texto: Even though is more emphatic than although (es: aun cuando, a pesar de que). Though, at the end of a sentence, is like an informal “however”: It was expensive. Good, though.

items: Never “despite of”: it is despite or in spite of.
Although is not combined with but in the same sentence (a copy of Spanish “aunque…, pero”).
However does not join two clauses with just a comma: a full stop or a semicolon is needed.
Even if (concession about a hypothesis) is not even though (concession about a real fact).

ejemplos.frase: Even though he had a map, he got lost.
ejemplos.traduccion: Aunque tenía un mapa, se perdió.

ejemplos.frase: In spite of the high price, the tickets sold out in minutes.
ejemplos.traduccion: A pesar del precio elevado, las entradas se agotaron en minutos.

ejemplos.frase: Despite having little experience, she got the job.
ejemplos.traduccion: A pesar de tener poca experiencia, consiguió el trabajo.

ejemplos.frase: Exports rose by 5%, whereas imports fell slightly.
ejemplos.traduccion: Las exportaciones subieron un 5 %, mientras que las importaciones bajaron ligeramente.

ejemplos.frase: The plan was risky. Nevertheless, the board approved it.
ejemplos.traduccion: El plan era arriesgado. No obstante, el consejo lo aprobó.

ejemplos.frase: The hotel was old, yet surprisingly comfortable.
ejemplos.traduccion: El hotel era viejo y, sin embargo, sorprendentemente cómodo.

errores_hispanohablantes.mal: Although it was late, but we kept working.
errores_hispanohablantes.bien: Although it was late, we kept working.
errores_hispanohablantes.nota: Although and but are not combined in the same sentence.

errores_hispanohablantes.mal: Despite of the traffic, we arrived on time.
errores_hispanohablantes.bien: Despite the traffic, we arrived on time.
errores_hispanohablantes.nota: Despite does not take of; in spite of does.

errores_hispanohablantes.mal: Despite it was cold, we swam.
errores_hispanohablantes.bien: Although it was cold, we swam.
errores_hispanohablantes.nota: Despite goes with a noun or -ing; for a clause, use although or despite the fact that.

ejercicios.frase: In spite ___ the noise, the baby slept all night.
respuestas: of
ejercicios.explicacion: This is the table row despite / in spite of + noun: the complete expression is in spite of. The clue is In spite ___ followed by the noise, a noun. The missing word is of; only despite does without it.
ejercicios.explicacion_breve: The expression is in spite of.
ejercicios.traduccion: A pesar del ruido, el bebé durmió toda la noche.

errores_previstos.respuesta: from
errores_previstos.explicacion: Wrong copy: the fixed preposition of the expression is of, in spite of.

errores_previstos.respuesta: to
errores_previstos.explicacion: In spite to does not exist; the expression is in spite of.

ejercicios.enunciado: Complete with the correct form of the verb.
ejercicios.frase: Despite ___ (train) hard, he didn't win the race.
respuestas: training
having trained
ejercicios.explicacion: The table shows that despite is followed by a noun or an -ing form. The clue is Despite followed directly by a verb: it must take -ing, training. Having trained, the perfect form, is also correct; it stresses that the training happened before the race.
ejercicios.traduccion: A pesar de entrenar mucho, no ganó la carrera.

errores_previstos.respuesta: train
errores_previstos.explicacion: After despite, which works as a preposition, the verb takes -ing, not the infinitive.

errores_previstos.respuesta: he trained
errores_previstos.explicacion: Despite cannot go with a clause; you would need despite the fact that he trained.

errores_previstos.respuesta: to train
errores_previstos.explicacion: After a preposition we do not use to + infinitive, but -ing.

ejercicios.frase: The film had excellent reviews. ___, I found it boring.
respuestas: However
Nevertheless
Nonetheless
ejercicios.explicacion: This is the row for however / nevertheless / nonetheless: connectors that start a new sentence, after a full stop, followed by a comma. The clue is the full stop before the gap, the comma after it and the contrast between the good reviews and the personal opinion. All three words are correct; nevertheless and nonetheless are more formal.
ejercicios.explicacion_breve: A connector that starts a new sentence, followed by a comma.
ejercicios.traduccion: La película tuvo críticas excelentes. Sin embargo, a mí me pareció aburrida.

errores_previstos.respuesta: Although
errores_previstos.explicacion: Although needs a subordinate clause and is not followed by a comma when it starts a sentence like this.

errores_previstos.respuesta: But
errores_previstos.explicacion: But coordinates within the same sentence; after a full stop and with a comma, the correct word is however.

errores_previstos.respuesta: Despite
errores_previstos.explicacion: Despite needs a noun or -ing after it, not a comma.

glosario.definicion_l: a new appraisal or evaluation · an essay or article that gives a critical evaluation (as of a book or play)

ejercicios.frase: Despite the ___ that she was exhausted, she finished the marathon.
respuestas: fact
ejercicios.explicacion: The table includes despite the fact that + subject + verb, the way to use despite with a complete clause. The clue is Despite the ___ that followed by she was exhausted, a clause. The missing word is fact.
ejercicios.traduccion: A pesar de que estaba agotada, terminó el maratón.

errores_previstos.respuesta: way
errores_previstos.explicacion: Despite the way that does not express concession; the fixed formula is despite the fact that.

errores_previstos.respuesta: reason
errores_previstos.explicacion: Despite the reason that does not exist; we say despite the fact that.

glosario.definicion_l: wear out completely · use up (resources or materials)

ejercicios.frase: ___ he earns a good salary, he never has any money.
respuestas: Even though
ejercicios.explicacion: The table shows that although, though and even though are followed by subject + verb. The clue is he earns a good salary, a complete clause. Even though is also more emphatic, and it fits the paradox of earning well and having no money. Despite and in spite of would need a noun or -ing.
ejercicios.explicacion_breve: It is followed by a clause (he earns…): even though.
ejercicios.traduccion: Aunque gana un buen sueldo, nunca tiene dinero.

por_opcion.Even though: Correct: it is followed by a clause and expresses an emphatic concession.
por_opcion.Despite: Incorrect: it cannot go with a clause; you would have to say despite earning.
por_opcion.In spite of: Incorrect: like despite, it needs a noun or -ing.
por_opcion.However: Incorrect: it starts a new sentence after a full stop and does not introduce a subordinate clause.

ejercicios.frase: Some people prefer tea, ___ others can't start the day without coffee.
respuestas: whereas
ejercicios.explicacion: This is whereas / while from the table: a contrast between two facts within the same sentence, followed by subject + verb. The clue is the opposition between two groups (some people / others) and the fact that the gap comes after a comma, in the middle of the sentence. However cannot join two clauses with just a comma.
ejercicios.explicacion_breve: Contrast between two groups within the same sentence: whereas.
ejercicios.traduccion: Algunas personas prefieren el té, mientras que otras no pueden empezar el día sin café.

por_opcion.whereas: Correct: it compares two opposite facts within the same sentence.
por_opcion.despite: Incorrect: it needs a noun or -ing, not a clause.
por_opcion.however: Incorrect: this unit warns that however does not join two clauses with just a comma; a full stop or a semicolon would be needed.

ejercicios.frase: We enjoyed the trip ___ the bad weather.
respuestas: despite
ejercicios.explicacion: This applies the table: despite is followed by a noun. The clue is the bad weather, a noun with no verb. Although and even though would need a clause (although the weather was bad), and whereas compares two facts; it does not express concession.
ejercicios.explicacion_breve: It is followed by a noun (the bad weather): despite.
ejercicios.traduccion: Disfrutamos del viaje a pesar del mal tiempo.

por_opcion.despite: Correct: followed by a noun, “in spite of”.
por_opcion.although: Incorrect: it needs a clause with a verb.
por_opcion.even though: Incorrect: it also needs a subject and a verb.
por_opcion.whereas: Incorrect: it contrasts two facts; it does not express that something happens in spite of an obstacle.

ejercicios.frase: I'll go to the beach ___ it rains; I don't care.
respuestas: even if
ejercicios.explicacion: The list in this unit distinguishes even if, a concession about a hypothesis, from even though, a concession about a real fact. The clue is that the rain is not a fact but a future possibility (Spanish “aunque llueva”, with the subjunctive), and I don't care. That is why even if is used, followed by the present with future meaning.
ejercicios.traduccion: Iré a la playa aunque llueva; me da igual.

por_opcion.even if: Correct: a hypothetical concession, “whether or not it rains”.
por_opcion.even though: Incorrect: it would present the rain as a real fact (although it is raining), which does not fit an uncertain future.
por_opcion.despite: Incorrect: it needs a noun or -ing, not a clause.

ejercicios.frase: Despite of his age, he runs every morning.
respuestas: Despite his age, he runs every morning.
In spite of his age, he runs every morning.
ejercicios.explicacion: This is the first warning in the list: never despite of. The clue is “Despite of”, a copy of Spanish “a pesar de”. Correct it by removing of (Despite his age) or by using the complete expression with of (In spite of his age); both are correct.
ejercicios.traduccion: A pesar de su edad, sale a correr todas las mañanas.

errores_previstos.respuesta: Despite of his age, he runs every morning.
errores_previstos.explicacion: This leaves the sentence uncorrected: despite never takes of.

errores_previstos.respuesta: In spite his age, he runs every morning.
errores_previstos.explicacion: In spite needs of: in spite of his age.

errores_previstos.respuesta: Although his age, he runs every morning.
errores_previstos.explicacion: Although needs a clause with a verb, not a noun.

ejercicios.frase: Although the hotel was expensive, but the rooms were small.
respuestas: Although the hotel was expensive, the rooms were small.
The hotel was expensive, but the rooms were small.
ejercicios.explicacion: The list in this unit rules out combining although and but in the same sentence, a copy of Spanish “aunque…, pero”. There are two corrections: remove but and keep although, or remove although and keep but as coordination. Both express the same contrast between the price and the size.
ejercicios.explicacion_breve: Although and but do not go together.
ejercicios.traduccion: Aunque el hotel era caro, las habitaciones eran pequeñas.

errores_previstos.respuesta: Although the hotel was expensive, but the rooms were small.
errores_previstos.explicacion: This leaves the sentence uncorrected: although and but do not go together.

errores_previstos.respuesta: Despite the hotel was expensive, the rooms were small.
errores_previstos.explicacion: Despite cannot be followed by a clause.

errores_previstos.respuesta: The hotel was expensive, however the rooms were small.
errores_previstos.explicacion: However does not join two clauses with just a comma; a full stop or a semicolon would be needed.

ejercicios.frase: In spite of it was late, they kept talking.
respuestas: Although it was late, they kept talking.
Even though it was late, they kept talking.
In spite of the fact that it was late, they kept talking.
Though it was late, they kept talking.
ejercicios.explicacion: This is the mistake from this unit of using despite or in spite of with a clause. The clue is it was late, which has a subject and a verb. Correct it by changing the connector to one that takes a clause (although, even though, though) or by adding the fact that (in spite of the fact that). All these options are accepted.
ejercicios.explicacion_breve: Before a clause, although or in spite of the fact that is needed.

errores_previstos.respuesta: In spite of it was late, they kept talking.
errores_previstos.explicacion: This leaves the sentence uncorrected: in spite of cannot go with a clause.

errores_previstos.respuesta: Despite it was late, they kept talking.
errores_previstos.explicacion: Changing in spite of to despite does not fix anything: it has the same grammar.

errores_previstos.respuesta: Although it was late, but they kept talking.
errores_previstos.explicacion: The connector is fixed, but but is added, and it does not combine with although.

ejercicios.enunciado: Rewrite the sentence starting with Despite.
ejercicios.frase: Although she was tired, she went to the party.
respuestas: Despite being tired, she went to the party.
Despite her tiredness, she went to the party.
Despite the fact that she was tired, she went to the party.
ejercicios.explicacion: The table gives three options after despite: -ing (Despite being tired), a noun (Despite her tiredness) or the fact that + clause (Despite the fact that she was tired). The clause she was tired must be changed into one of these forms; all three are correct. What you cannot do is copy the clause after despite.
ejercicios.explicacion_breve: Despite + -ing, + noun or + the fact that.
ejercicios.traduccion: A pesar de estar cansada, fue a la fiesta.

errores_previstos.respuesta: Despite she was tired, she went to the party.
errores_previstos.explicacion: Despite does not take a clause with a finite verb.

errores_previstos.respuesta: Despite of being tired, she went to the party.
errores_previstos.explicacion: Despite never takes of.

errores_previstos.respuesta: Despite be tired, she went to the party.
errores_previstos.explicacion: After despite the verb takes -ing: being tired.

glosario.definicion_l: temporary loss of strength and energy resulting from hard physical or mental work

ejercicios.enunciado: Join the two sentences into one starting with Although.
ejercicios.frase: The car is old. It runs perfectly.
respuestas: Although the car is old, it runs perfectly.
Although it is old, the car runs perfectly.
Although the car's old, it runs perfectly.
Although it's old, the car runs perfectly.
ejercicios.explicacion: Although introduces the concessive clause, the obstacle (the car is old), and the other clause becomes the main clause; the full stop disappears and is replaced by a comma. The noun the car can go in the first or the second clause, with the pronoun it in the other, and contracted forms are accepted. What does not change is that although goes with the obstacle.
ejercicios.explicacion_breve: Although introduces the concessive clause and the full stop disappears.
ejercicios.traduccion: Aunque el coche es viejo, funciona perfectamente.

errores_previstos.respuesta: Although the car is old, but it runs perfectly.
errores_previstos.explicacion: Although and but are not combined.

errores_previstos.respuesta: Although the car runs perfectly, it is old.
errores_previstos.explicacion: Although must go with the obstacle (being old), not with what happens in spite of it; otherwise the meaning changes.

glosario.definicion_l: a score in baseball made by a runner touching all four bases safely · the act of testing something

respuestas: in spite of the rain
ejercicios.explicacion: This is the expression in spite of + noun from the table. The fixed order is in + spite + of, followed by the noun with its article, the rain. It is not a complete sentence but the phrase that could start one (In spite of the rain, we went out).

errores_previstos.respuesta: in the spite of rain
errores_previstos.explicacion: The fixed expression has no article: in spite of; the goes with rain.

errores_previstos.respuesta: spite in of the rain
errores_previstos.explicacion: The fixed order is in spite of.

respuestas: even though I knew it
ejercicios.explicacion: This is the row although / though / even though + subject + verb. Even though is a single unit (even before though) and is followed by the clause: subject (I) + verb (knew) + object (it). The whole is a concessive subordinate clause (es: “aun sabiéndolo”).

errores_previstos.respuesta: even though it knew I
errores_previstos.explicacion: The subject is I and it goes before the verb; it is the object and goes at the end: I knew it.

errores_previstos.respuesta: even though knew I it
errores_previstos.explicacion: After the connector comes normal clause order: subject + verb, I knew it.

descripcion_larga_es: Contrast and concession connectors express that something happens in spite of an obstacle or that two facts are opposed. They are distinguished by what follows them: although and even though go with a clause; despite and in spite of, with a noun or -ing; however and nevertheless start a new sentence; whereas and while compare two facts. Spanish speakers find this hard because Spanish “aunque” and “a pesar de” allow structures that are not correct in English.

contexto.que_es: It is the set of connectors that express concession (something happens in spite of something else) and contrast (two opposite facts). The grammatical key is what follows: a clause with subject and verb (although, even though, whereas, despite the fact that), a noun or -ing (despite, in spite of) or a new sentence after a full stop or semicolon (however, nevertheless, nonetheless).
contexto.por_que_importa: Concession is essential for arguing with nuance: acknowledging an objection and keeping your position. A B2-level exam assesses both the variety of connectors and their accuracy, and mistakes such as despite of, although… but or however joined with just a comma are always penalised. The nuances also matter: even if (hypothesis) is not even though (real fact).
contexto.cuando_se_usa: In argumentative essays, reports, letters of complaint and oral presentations. The signal is the logical relation (an obstacle that does not prevent something, or two opposite facts) and the structure of what follows. Spanish speakers copy “aunque…, pero”, translate “a pesar de que” as despite and join sentences with however and a comma.
